text: If we would guide by the light of reason, we must let our minds be bold.
author: Louis D. Brandeis
role: Justice, Supreme Court of the United States
source: Dissenting opinion, New State Ice Co. v. Liebmann, 285 U.S. 262 (1932). law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/285/262
sourceShort: New State Ice Co. v. Liebmann (1932)

text: Fear of serious injury cannot alone justify suppression of free speech and assembly. Men feared witches and burnt women. It is the function of speech to free men from the bondage of irrational fears.
author: Louis D. Brandeis
role: Justice, Supreme Court of the United States
source: Concurring opinion, Whitney v. California, 274 U.S. 357 (1927). law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/274/357

text: A word is not a crystal, transparent and unchanged, it is the skin of a living thought and may vary greatly in color and content according to the circumstances and the time in which it is used.
author: Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr.
role: Justice, Supreme Court of the United States
source: Opinion of the Court, Towne v. Eisner, 245 U.S. 418 (1918). law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/245/418

text: Narrowed as its function is in this manner, the judiciary does not pass upon questions of wisdom, justice or expediency of legislation.
author: Jose P. Laurel
role: Justice, Supreme Court of the Philippines
source: Angara v. Electoral Commission, G.R. No. 45081, July 15, 1936 (63 Phil. 139). lawphil.net/judjuris/juri1936/jul1936/gr_45081_1936.html

text: The policy of the courts is to avoid ruling on constitutional questions and to presume that the acts of the political departments are valid in the absence of a clear and unmistakable showing to the contrary. To doubt is to sustain.
author: Cruz, J.
source: Garcia v. Executive Secretary, G.R. No. 100883, December 2, 1991. lawphil.net/judjuris/juri1991/dec1991/gr_100883_1991.html

text: What is at stake here is whether Filipinos or foreigners will have effective control of the Philippine national economy.
author: Antonio T. Carpio
role: Justice, Supreme Court of the Philippines
source: Resolution, Gamboa v. Teves, G.R. No. 176579, October 9, 2012. lawphil.net/judjuris/juri2012/oct2012/gr_176579_2012.html

text: Let us have faith that right makes might, and in that faith, let us, to the end, dare to do our duty as we understand it.
author: Abraham Lincoln
source: Address at Cooper Union, New York, 27 February 1860, as printed in The Collected Works of Abraham Lincoln, ed. Roy P. Basler (closing sentence; the printed text sets it in capitals for emphasis). Text read at Abraham Lincoln Online: abrahamlincolnonline.org/lincoln/speeches/cooper.htm

text: I have cherished the ideal of a democratic and free society in which all persons live together in harmony and with equal opportunities. It is an ideal which I hope to live for and to achieve.
author: Nelson Mandela
source: Statement from the dock, Rivonia Trial, Pretoria, 20 April 1964 (two consecutive sentences, no cut). Wording as quoted from the typescript by the Nelson Mandela Foundation: nelsonmandela.org/news/entry/i-am-prepared-to-die . Another transcription (Wikisource) reads "to see realised" instead of "to achieve".
sourceShort: Statement from the dock, Rivonia Trial (1964)

text: I had learnt the true practice of law. I had learnt to find out the better side of human nature and to enter men's hearts. I realized that the true function of a lawyer was to unite parties riven asunder.
author: Mahatma Gandhi
role: Lawyer and leader of India's independence movement
source: An Autobiography (The Story of My Experiments with Truth), Part II, Chapter XIV, "Preparation for the Case" (three consecutive sentences, no cut). Checked in two editions: mkgandhi-sarvodaya.org/autobio/chap39.htm and standardebooks.org/ebooks/mahatma-gandhi/the-story-of-my-experiments-with-truth/mahadev-desai/text/chapter-2-14

text: Effective participation by members of all racial and ethnic groups in the civic life of our Nation is essential if the dream of one Nation, indivisible, is to be realized.
author: O'Connor, J.
role: Justice, Supreme Court of the United States
source: Opinion of the Court, Grutter v. Bollinger, 539 U.S. 306 (decided 23 June 2003); one sentence, footnote number left out. law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/539/306

text: Our whole constitutional heritage rebels at the thought of giving government the power to control men's minds.
author: Marshall, J.
role: Justice, Supreme Court of the United States
source: Opinion of the Court, Stanley v. Georgia, 394 U.S. 557 (decided 7 April 1969); one sentence, footnote number left out. law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/394/557

text: The government of the United States has been emphatically termed a government of laws, and not of men. It will certainly cease to deserve this high appellation, if the laws furnish no remedy for the violation of a vested legal right.
author: Marshall, C.J.
role: Chief Justice, Supreme Court of the United States
source: Opinion of the Court, Marbury v. Madison, 5 U.S. (1 Cranch) 137 (1803); two consecutive sentences, footnote number left out. law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/5/137

text: ... in our adversary system of criminal justice, any person haled into court, who is too poor to hire a lawyer, cannot be assured a fair trial unless counsel is provided for him. This seems to us to be an obvious truth.
author: Black, J.
role: Justice, Supreme Court of the United States
source: Opinion of the Court, Gideon v. Wainwright, 372 U.S. 335 (decided 18 March 1963). The "..." only leaves out the opening words of the sentence ("Not only these precedents but also reason and reflection require us to recognize that"); the rest is two consecutive sentences. law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/372/335

text: No official, no matter how high, is above the law. The courts are the forum which functionate to safeguard individual liberty and to punish official transgressors.
author: Malcolm, J.
role: Justice, Supreme Court of the Philippines
source: Villavicencio v. Lukban, G.R. No. L-14639, 25 March 1919 (two consecutive sentences; "functionate" is as printed). lawphil.net/judjuris/juri1919/mar1919/gr_l-14639_1919.html
